summary: Sisir Roy works in philosophy and other fields. He studied under Debabrata SenSharma and held posts as Professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies, both attested in 2009.
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti. Kwan also studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005.

So Takahashi (b. 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He served at Meijo University as an Associate Professor (attested 1977-1978) and Professor (attested 1991).

Sodo Mori (b. 1934) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957-1968), working in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Japanese representative for the Pali Text Society (~1980) and held a professorship at Aichi Gakuin University (~1989-2005).
Sodo Yokoyama (1907-1980) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Eiko Hashimoto and Kodo Sawaki (~1940-1965), and later taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Shaku (1860-1919) studied at Keio University (~1882-1885) and under Kosen Imakita (~1878-1892). Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he became chief abbot at Engaku-ji in 1892 and held a post at Hanazono University.
Sogen Omori (1904-1994) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who taught Tenshin Tanouye. He held posts at Kōho-in Temple (~1953-1994) and Hanazono University (~1978-1982).

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947-2019) studied at the University of Delhi (~1967-1970) and Cambridge (1971), as well as under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Nyoshul Khenpo. He founded Rigpa in 1975.

Soiku Shigematsu (b. 1943) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1961-1965) and under Kiju Shigematsu. Working in Buddhist studies and other fields, he held posts at Kansai Medical University (~1968-1975) and Shizuoka University (~1975-2008).
Sojo Hirano (1930-1999) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Sonja Arntzen. Hirano held posts at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992-1996).

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served as a Departmental Lecturer at Oxford and held a research post at the CNRS (attested 2019).

Somadeva Vasudeva earned a PhD at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. An Indologist, he held posts at the Institut Français de Pondichéry, Columbia University as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit, and Kyoto University as Professor in 2011.

Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a Master's in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2006), supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat with Watchara Ngamchitcharoen on his committee.

Sonam Chhoki is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Gyatso (b. 1933) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shinjo Kawasaki. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko and as a Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Kachru completed a PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. Working in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Kachru has held fellowships at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and Forum Transregionale Studien.

Sonam Thakchoe works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1998-2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, and held a post there around 2005.

Sonam Tsering is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral supervision under Gray Tuttle. Tsering also studied under Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Gyumé Khenzur Lobzang Trinlé.

Songeun Choe works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and earned a PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).
